method.release_time: summary.microbatch_metrics.layer_metrics.io_start_time_ms; layer 1..7 only, verified equal to preceding layer compute_start_ms
method.group: npu0..15 and16..31; kth admitted long request per NPU, k is 1-based
method.ideal_prefix: sum full compute of every preceding request in that NPU executed order; at layer l add (l-1)*long layer C. Across a fixed group/k the long contributions are identical, so prefix spread comes from short population prefix only.
method.residual: actual release - ideal_prefix; includes earlier stalls and any idle, not an SSD service duration. Range terms are not additive.
method.warm_row_rule: mean of the 16 actual release times inside [2000,4000)
method.limitations: Observational phase diagnostic, not a unique causal identification. Same-k random groups need not be real simultaneous cohorts.
method.circular_coherence: abs(mean(exp(2*pi*i*release/long_C))); 1 is alignment modulo the long compute period, 0 is dispersed. Addresses full-span multiples-of-period ambiguity, not an I/O congestion metric.

conclusion: Approximate cohort is initially aligned but spreads over repeated long requests. Long layers1..7 have zero barrier stall and preserve each kth-cohort spread. Across-request actual spread greatly exceeds the bounded 5-12 ms pure-compute-prefix spread in the structured order; accumulated short stalls plus long layer0 stalls cause the extra timing residual, with measured idle zero. This is observational support for loss of synchronization, not unique proof of the small U difference.
